title: When do Mixed-Integer Games Admit Rational Equilibria?
summary: We consider mixed-integer linear-quadratic generalized Nash equilibrium problems, i.e., games in which each player solves a mixed-integer program subject to linear constraints in her own and rivals' strategies as well as an objective which is quadratic in her own strategies and bilinear in her own and rivals' strategies. For this class of games, we study the question of the existence of rational equilibria assuming rational input data.
